Since olden days, against the sun's whims

Sorry, but at home I'd like to rest easy,

Leave me be.
Please, leave me be.

Well, come in.

There's nothing here but my painting things.
What are you doing here?
I'm a landscape painter, you see.
I paint here by the river like this.

Cold every day, isn't it.
Have you heard, young fellow?
There's a killer by the name of Jack prowling
about these parts
I was sketching here by the river

Even I got quite a fright, I'll admit.
You once found a body around here.

Are you not afraid of the killer?
Bah, the culprit won't bother with a shabby
old man like me.
Besides, I can't bring myself to abandon

Have you no family?
Family, eh...
I had a wife, and children too
Fully aware how selfish it is, I wander alone

An artist has to do battle with all

Well, well, so you've come.

if you can barely eat, you're poor.

en: I wonder what kind of face the fiend has.
Me, I'm curious.
Truth is, I was painting until recently.
Then out of the blue I placed in a contest,
and everyone hailed it as a masterpiece.
After that, painting became torture.
Could I ever top the praise for my first work?
The worry just ate at me.
So I took the plunge and became a sculptor,

Now I'm able to create my work

Yes
What's going on?
I didn't sense you at all...
No, never mind that.
Why have you come here at this hour?
I was interested in your work.
Suddenly I just had to see it.
I'm interested in you, too.
I've been thinking I'd like to sculpt you.
Your outward beauty is one reason, sure,
but that alone won't do for a model of mine.
It's the mystery hidden within that draws me.
Are you a good person?

Yes, I suppose I'm not.

en: Waah! Wh-what are you doing
Living on by taking others' lives like this,
I'm evil after all
aren't I...

Ouch, there's a bruise on my back

en: I am not fond of mornings.
Oh dear. That is a problem.
Then you'd never be given important work.
Ah, my apologies if that sounded rude.
(Hmph... Labor? How absurd.)
Oh, we meet again.
Quite the early riser, aren't you?
So 'bad at mornings' was just modesty.
I don't know what work you do, but every day
you work so hard. You seem a diligent man.
I wish London were full of people as diligent
and refined as you, I truly do.
Could you tell me the time?
My watch has stopped.
Oh, that must be a nuisance.
It's too dark to see. Hold it up to the lamp
and have a look.
That helps. You have my thanks.
Not at all, I'm glad to be of use.
Not knowing the time is such a bother.
Without an orderly life, people
grow utterly slack.
I would have your name.
I'm nobody of any importance
My name is Justin.
I've long worked at the bank just up ahead.
Good evening. We meet again.
How are you doing?
As for me, nothing has changed.
I work away steadily, day after day.
Banking demands honesty and precision.
Why, how nice, we meet again.
You work so hard every day.
Is it not you who has it hard?
No, no. Being trusted with work is, to me,
a matter of pride.
My family has lived here in London
for generations, so I always want to do
what's best for this city.
Welcome. How may I help you?
A deposit, perhaps?
About this thing called a bank account,
I would like to ask...
What must I do?
Well, this is a surprise.
A customer opening his first bank account...
Very well, allow me to explain.
I'm not used to civilized society, you see.
Surely you jest.
You strike me as a fine gentleman.
I'm Justin. Pleased to meet you.
I'm obliged to you.
A deposit, perhaps?... Oh. Hello.
It's you. We must be fated to meet.
When someone I know comes to the bank,
it makes me very happy.
I'll gladly help with anything you need.
Please come again.
Welcome. I've been expecting you.
What can I do for you today?
I had hoped you might tell me
a little more...
Am I intruding?
No, no, not at all
It gets hectic at midday, of course, but
I'm glad you came by.
I can also advise you on deposits, so
please come again.
, welcome.
Thank you, as always.
It's a stuffy place, but please be at ease.
Few people can relax in a bank, I suppose.
I'm always on my guard at work, too.
It is tiring, I admit.
My work keeps me on my toes. It's tiring.
I wish to be diligent, but
now and then I'd like to take it easy, too.
Shall we talk away from work next time?
I'd like a good long talk with you.
Hm? Who might you be?
Pardon me, have we met before?
No. I seem to have the wrong house.
My apologies.
Ah, I see.
Don't worry about it. It's quite all right.
Oh. You've come again?
If you have no business, I'll excuse myself.
, it's you!
The bank also handles loan inquiries.
If you need one, just ask at the bank.
Please don't hesitate to come by.
, good day to you.
Why not come in for a while?
I'd like a friendship outside of work.
I'm surrounded by such stiff, formal people.
Come by whenever you like.
You'll always be welcome.
Humans are such empty, foolish creatures
What good is working so hard?
I'll give you work worth doing,
as my servant... Hahahaha.
What a lovely morning. A day like this

I'm ashamed to admit it, but I'm just

Might I ask your name?

I'm not used to civilized society.

Sorry, I just stopped by today

Though I've been messing up a lot lately

Boats?
I run a boat-hire business.

A boat trip down the river is a real treat.
Rowing down the Thames... it's great fun.
Good evening. Hi there.

I started hiring out boats for pocket money,
but it barely pays.
I wonder what I'm doing wrong.
Good evening. We do keep meeting.

Seems I botched the repair
I just can't seem to earn any more

No, I was merely passing by.
O-oh, I see

Sigh... I'm not making any money
Sigh

I've lost the confidence to keep this job up

Oh, what am I going to do

but the way things are, it's just

Maybe I should go borrow money from the bank

not here. That would suit me better.
Why not take a boat out while you're here?
Hello. How are things with you?
Not so great on my end.
But I'll manage somehow.
No use getting discouraged, after all.
I need the money.
Rather than toil at work that earns you nothing,
I shall offer you a better choice...
Become my servant.
Now your power surpasses any human's.
From now on, fretting over such petty things
is something you would do well to give up.
Yes, it is. By the way
that's quite a big load you're carrying.
I see, so that's what it is.
Good luck with your work.
Boats? What line of work are you in?
No, I'm sorry, but I was only passing
by. No boat for me, thank you.
Yes, one of these days.

, my master. Your orders...

Command me as you will...

Trouble is, I can't treat my own back.
Oh, what's wrong? Here to see the doctor?
You look pale. Does it hurt anywhere?
No. I am sturdier than I look.
Really? Somehow you still look a bit
under the weather to me.
I'm Quentin, a physician.
Come by whenever you feel unwell.
We're only human. Don't overdo it.
(As if one such as I could ever fall ill.)
Are you coming down with a cold or something?
You do look pale, you know.
You still look rather pale. What do you say,
shall I examine you while you're here?
No, thank you.
Talking with you is one thing, but
I have never cared for hospitals.
Is that so? Ha ha ha ha.
But that won't do.
You'll ruin your health one day.
Good of you to come. Hello.
Hmm, you seem to be in good health, so
you must just be pale by nature.
I may have troubled you by pushing
an examination on you. Forgive me.
Though I think most doctors would make
the same mistake.
Are you keeping well?
There's a cold going around London lately.
Do take care of yourself.
Lately more people in town are looking pale.
Whatever could be the matter...
You're white as a sheet! An emergency?
I'll see emergencies at any hour.
No, it seems I have come to the wrong place.

Come to me whenever you're feeling unwell.
Oh, hello. How are you feeling?

With dreadful crimes and a strange illness,

I just came to pay my respects.
I may not look it, but I'm the hardy sort.

I don't mind just talking with you, but
the truth is, I'm not good with doctors.
What a surprising weakness. That won't do.
You'll ruin your health that way.
No, I've come to the wrong place. Sorry.

Come in. You're most welcome.
He alone has noticed the change in everyone.
No one but him would ever notice.
Yes, if only he weren't here...
I can't let him find out.
There's no other way.
You'll have to become
my servant.

en: They say God judges the sins of men...
But then who will judge ours...
I beg you, let your Wilfred serve you.

I will do anything...

Judging by your fine attire...
you're not here to pawn anything.
Ah, I know. You're interested in antiques?

I see, I see.
Please, take your time and look around.
Drop by often, and you might just
find a real treasure.
Thank you for visiting our shop, sir.
Always so distinguished. I'm most impressed.
Do antiques interest you, sir?
We have a fine stock of rare pieces.
When something rare comes in, I'll let you know.
Welcome, sir.
Well now, what are you looking for today?
Times are hard, so some folk are selling off
antiques so precious you'd hardly believe it.
Now's your chance.
We're really a pawnshop, you know,
but we've long doubled as an antique shop.
It started as my old man's hobby,
but I built it up into a real business.
What do you think?
You'd be surprised what wonderful pieces
hide among common folk's pawned goods.
I get them for a song, and then...
Oops, I shouldn't have said that.
Isn't it time? Won't you choose a piece
to add to your collection?
I'm always glad to help.
Who is it?
Here to pawn? We're closed at this hour.
The antique shop's only open by day, too.
Please come during business hours.
Many thanks for your patronage, as ever.
What brings you here at this hour...
Something to discuss in private?
For you, sir, I could let my best pieces
go a little cheaper.
But that's our secret.
Welcome, sir, so good of you to come.
It's just me and my doddering old father, but do come in.
I was just hoping for a nice long chat
about antiques with you, sir. I'm delighted.
And do drop by the shop, too!
Foolish human, blinded by greed.
Once you are my servant, your greed will fade.
What a kindness I've done him, if I say so myself.
Hahahaha...
How very amusing!
note: follows #4487 after a pause on the same line (player laughing)

en: What can I do for you, young sir?
No, I only came to look around today.
If I find something I like, I'll buy it, though.
You always look so very distinguished.
Young as you are, you like antiques, sir?
Though if I see something I like, I'll take it.
I'll obey your orders, even at the cost of my life...
Hack, hack... My whole body aches...
It's agony...
, my master. As you wish...
note: after the name, servant mode as #0

en: I feel so sluggish, and my whole body aches.
Perhaps my time is drawing near...
Oh... Welcome.
What might you be looking for?
No, I've only come to look today.
Standing is hard on an old man, so
I'll just sit myself down in this chair.
Do call me if you need anything.
How good of you to come.
Please, browse the shop at your leisure.
Yes, I'll do that.
Is the other half of the shop a pawnshop?
That's right. My son runs it.
Lazy and greedy, he's a good-for-nothing.
He even pokes his nose into this shop of mine.
It's truly shameful.
Has my son Will been causing you trouble
lately? I'm terribly sorry.
Please forgive him, for this old man's sake.
And don't let it keep you from the shop.
I'm an old man, you see, so I never even
go out. Meeting customers like you is
my one and only pleasure.
I'm grateful just to have you visit.
I do hope you'll keep coming back.
Good day. What brings you here?
The antique shop is only open by day.
I'd be glad if you came in opening hours.
That work's hard on an old man, too...
Let's meet at the shop around midday.
Why, it's you, sir. Thank you as always.
I'm sorry, but I can't open the shop
outside opening hours...
And it seems my fool of a son has been
causing you trouble. I'm terribly sorry.
I beg you, please forgive him.
Oh, my faithful customer...
Would you care for some tea?
I hope we'll see you again.
Hello. I'll just have a little look around.
Yes, of course.
Thank you. I'll do just that.
So the other half of the shop is a pawnshop.
Oh, my faithful customer... Thank you
so much. Would you care for some tea?
If an old man's company suits you, that is.
Even an old man like this...
must I take him with my own hands...?
I have to do this.
That much is certain.
But I wonder... for us, who must do this,
isn't our existence as vampires
unforgivable
in and of itself...?
The jewels we carry here are all
pieces favoured by nobles and royalty,
every last one of them.
Please, take your time and look them over.
Sir, might I suggest a ring from this case?
What do you think?
note: shared with Arthur msg 194557 after #4811

en: A diamond ring to grace a lady's slender
fingers ever so beautifully, sir.
Is it a present for your sweetheart?
It takes courage to express one's feelings,
but these jewels will help lend you
that courage...
Until you find a piece that pleases you,
please take your time and look around.
Have you made your choice?
I'll take this necklace.
This necklace sets off a lady's skin
most beautifully.
I'm fond of women with lovely throats...
Ah, is that so, sir?
A very... refined taste you have, sir.
We look forward to your next visit.
My apologies.
note: Next row #2565 starts with a capital ('We're already closed...'), so a full sentence here.

en: I'm afraid the shop is closed, so
A-a thief?!
What on earth has happened?
W-waaaaaaah...
Such beauty, and such coldness...
...A jewel is a dead, unmoving thing,
so why does it enthrall people so?
If she's your sweetheart, she must be
a charming lady indeed.
Until you find a piece that pleases you,
I'll take this ring.
My apologies.
note: Same as #4576.

en: At my master's command, I would give up
even my very life...
I can't really remember my family back home.
My head's in a fog every day, whatever I do.
Please, give me your orders. Come now...
By day I'm sluggish and can't move, but at
night my head's clear and I'm full of strength. Odd.
Ah, it's been ages since I talked to anyone.
Oh? And why is that...?
My name is Nick. I came here to London
to earn a living. My family's in the country,
and I work at the factory morning till night...
We shall meet again.
That match factory is where I work.
Good morning. Hello there.
Another full day at the factory today. Bye.
Good morning. Glad to see you looking well.
You must come from a wealthy family.
You always seem so at ease.
Toiling away every day as I do, I sometimes
find this life so empty...
You look unwell. What's the matter?
Oh, it's nothing.
I'm just worn out from nonstop work. Dizzy...
Why not go to a hospital and see
a doctor?
I've no time or money for that.
I came all the way from the country to work.
I can't go resting. My family...
Thank you for your kindness, but
I'll be fine... Goodbye now.
Oh, really, I'm fine...
Thanks for the other day. I'm managing
to keep working now, thanks to you.
Once I've saved up enough, I'd like to go
home. I hope that day comes soon.
Good evening. We do meet often, don't we?
You seem to have a busy job too.
It's odd for me of all people to say, but...
please do look after your health.
Ah, you mustn't go into the factory.
It's a match factory. We handle phosphorus,
so no one but staff may come in!
Phosphorus... A dangerous substance.
Unavoidable in a match factory, though.
Yes, phosphorus is poisonous.
Please go outside at once.
At this rate, the manager will scold me.
My apologies.
I shall take my leave.
Not at all. If you feel unwell, please be sure
to go to the hospital.
note: Completes #4639 (slice 057) '...please be sure'.

en: Ah, a match factory.
I see...
Please leave now. Phosphorus is poisonous.
You mustn't come here again.
Oh, honestly...
You're a worry. This factory handles
dangerous materials. It's no place to come
and go in fine clothes like those.
No, you needn't worry about me.
More to the point, how are you?
Yes, I'm well, thank you.
But you really are an odd one.
Either you're fearless, or you don't realize...
It's me who's worried sick.
! Here again?
I'm no longer surprised. You really do seem
far hardier than most people.
Even in this choking factory you carry on
as if it's nothing. It's a mystery.
I want to get back to my family soon.
For now, their monthly letter is my only joy.
Living alone in a big city like this,
working from dawn to dusk... it feels hollow.
Poor or not, I'd rather live with my family.
Hello...
What is it?
Sorry, I'm not feeling well just now...
Um, sorry, but could you come back later?
I have a terrible headache.
What brings you here?
You're always so well. I envy you.
By the time I get home I'm worn out,
and I don't feel like doing anything.
So at home, all I do is sleep.
Welcome. It's a shabby place, I'm afraid.
I don't even have time to clean or do laundry.
I miss my wife and children's faces.
You're welcome to come by any time.
Why ever is that?
I see. That must be hard.
Let's meet again some time. Goodbye.
Good evening. What's the matter?
Are you all right? You should see a doctor.
I see, so it's a match factory.
Don't be so nonchalant about it!
My apologies. I'll take my leave, then.
I'm sorry to have troubled you.
You... It's dangerous in here,
you mustn't just wander in.
You mustn't come here again, all right?
I was passing by, so I came to say hello.
Are you well? How is your health?
There you go again, so carefree.
I'm glad to hear it.
I appreciate your concern, but
I'm sturdy, if nothing else. I'll be fine.
Come now. It's me who's worried sick.
far hardier than most folk.
Hello. Excuse me.
note: Also Bruce, msg 223353 (he answers 'Yes. What can I do for you?').

en: and I can't bring myself to do anything.
How his family back home will grieve...
Nick... I'm sorry!
I'm sick of this fighting!
I must settle this soon... very soon...
My name is Arthur, a humble hairdresser.
I hope you'll remember me.
I am Arthur, a humble hairdresser.
you're out for a stroll?
note: After '{NAME}, sir,' (#2557); lowercase.

en: , sir,
your fine looks never fail to impress me.
I am a humble hairdresser
by the name of Arthur.
I'm Arthur. I work as a hairdresser.
, sir, please do visit
my shop again.
May I ask who you are?

note: After 'I am ' (#525) + name: 'I am {NAME}.'

en: I don't believe we've met.
My humble name is Arthur, and
I am a hairdresser by trade.
Are you wondering why a mere hairdresser
lives in a house like this?
The ladies of this city have been kind
enough to favour me, so I have a bit
put aside, you see.
Do come visit my beauty salon.
Please do visit the salon again, too.
After work, I make a point of resting
quietly at home.
The mornings are busy, you see.
How good of you to come.
I'll have tea prepared right away.
You even have servants.
Well, yes.
Thanks to my salon clients, I can now
afford a life of luxury.
With all my heart,
I shall see to your every need.
Good day, and welcome to the beauty salon.
I am Arthur, the hairdresser.
I am glad to say the salon is popular
with a great many noble ladies.
Of course,
clients other than ladies are welcome too.
If it interests you,
please do come again.
Welcome to the beauty salon.
Arthur the hairdresser, at your service.
My main work is dressing noble ladies' hair.
Curls hanging down at the sides of the face
are all the fashion now.
A noble princess famed throughout London,
Lady Rose of the Epstein family, wears her
hair this way too.
And you,
are a handsome man indeed...
The noble ladies who come here
talk of nothing but you.
Looking fine is not just for women,
you know,
All the more so for a handsome gentleman
such as yourself, sir.
One can never take too much care
over one's appearance.
How about having your hair curled,
I apply this curling iron to the hair
and twirl it into ringlets.
No, I think I shall decline.
We also have wigs for gentlemen.
Long hair tied back at the nape, say
I am fond of my hair as it is.
Do come by if you ever change your mind.
Then for today, allow me to give you
a beauty mask, perhaps.
I'm just about to set a lady's hair,
so please wait a moment.
There, madam, thank you for waiting.
Curls piled up high, set with pomade,
a dusting of hair powder, silk flowers
Lastly, a touch of perfume.
There, all done.
Madam, you look simply lovely.
When you go to bed, do wear
a nightcap.
How was the beauty mask the other day?
Well, it wasn't bad.
Then the same again today.
Today, too, I have prepared
a special facial treatment for you.
Lately, the noble ladies have all been
stolen from me by my client
Every last one of them...
Damn it. When I'm the one
who's the better-looking man...
Wh-why are
you here?
Th-that muttering just now was, um
Don't worry about it.
Today I thought I'd teach you my own
secrets of beauty.
Waaaaah... S-stop it!
M-my beautiful body... it's wounded...
Blood is what keeps me eternally young,
the very source of my life...
Far better than any facial mask.
You even have servants?
Thanks to my salon clients, I can now
talk of nothing but you.
note: Same as #4758.

en: Why not have that longish hair of yours curled?
note: Followed by #4559 'What do you think?'.

en: No, thank you.
I'll pass.
I'm happy with my hair as it is.
Yes, it was rather nice.
, my master. Welcome.
Just say the word!
So sleepy...
And Mum keeps scolding me, too. Hmph.
I want to be of use. Your orders...
More and more cuts... and I didn't do a thing.
Weird.
Whoa, whoa! Old man, out of the way!
Don't walk right in the middle of the road.
Oh, I'm sorry about that, sonny.
"Sonny"? How rude. I've got a job already.
I've got to get to work now. So busy!
Walking there is dangerous, you know.
Quite right. I shall be careful.
Work hard at your job.
Old man, you sound just like my mum.
See you!
Aren't you going to work, old man?
Morning, old man.
Looks like you've got time to spare. Lucky.
Grown-ups get more free time. So unfair.
Hey, old man. Taking it easy again today?
I may not look it, but I'm busy.
Mum's wages alone aren't enough to live on.
I bet you're from a good family, old man.
Do come chat with me sometime. Bye now.
note: Also Winifred (msg 275230); wording works for both.

en: Whoa, careful there, sonny.
You could take a nasty fall on a dark street.
Sorry, old man.
I was in a bit of a hurry. I'm starving.
I've got a job already, you know.
Don't you go to school?
School? That's for folks with time
and money. Nothing to do with me.
Mum and me, we both work to earn money.
Well, I'm in a hurry. See you!
I'm in a hurry, see. Bye!
Evening, old man.
We both got through another day's work.
Huh? But wait, do you even work, old man?
Hey, old man. Doing all right?
I'm worn out. I wanna get to bed.
Working at the factory is really tiring.
A bakery or a bookshop would be easier.
Huh? Who are you? What brings you here?
The manager isn't here, you know.
Mmh... What a dreadful smell.
Just what kind of factory is this, sonny?
That's mean. I'm Daniel, I'm 15.
Don't call me "sonny". I work here.
This factory makes glue.
The smell's strong, but you get used to it.
So, what can I do for you?
The smell is so foul, I forgot why I came.
I shall come back another time. Farewell.
Huh? Oh, it's you, old man.
Here for the manager? The boss isn't in.
So this is where you've been working...
Just what kind of factory is this?
So, what do you want?
The smell's no bother once you're used to it.
You again, old man?
Didn't you say the smell was awful?
No sightseeing, all right? We're serious here.
I get all sticky at work every day.
Even a bath won't get it off.
You're a real odd one, old man.
Since you're here, want to work with me?
Ahaha, kidding, kidding, it's a joke.
You can't do it in fancy clothes like those.
At work, the boss and older lads scold me,
and at home Mum nags me, tired from work.
But I don't really mind that stuff, you know.
Have you got a family, old man?
Guess not. You look so carefree.
But I bet a family makes you way happier.
Coming! Huh?
Who are you? My mother is out right now.
Please come back later.
Old man... you here to sell me something?
I'm just a kid, so I haven't got any money.
Old man, are you a policeman or a detective?
Let me help too! That'd be brilliant.
I don't think my mum would be much help.
Who wants to hear a middle-aged lady moan?
Hello, old man. Come on in.
It's a mess, but want some tea?
Though when I make tea, it smells of glue,
or so Mum grumbles.
You can come again if you like.
Oh dear, I'm sorry, sonny.
...Still, "old man"? That's harsh.
Calling me "sonny" is ruder, mister!
I've already got a job, you know.
I was just on my way to work.
Oh, I'm so busy.
Honestly, walking around there is dangerous,
mister.
You're right, I'll be careful.
Good luck with your work.
You sound just like my mum.
"Mister" doesn't suit you after all.
See you, old man!
Oh dear, back to "old man" again...
Oh, sorry. It's "mister", isn't it?
note: Follows slice 060 #4833 'Aren't you going to work, old man?'.

en: Good morning, old m... mister.
Hey, mister. Taking it easy again today?
I bet you're from a good family, mister.
"Old man", is it? That's harsh.
note: Answers slice 060 #4844 'Sorry, old man.'.

en: Aren't you on your way home from school?
School? That's for folks with time
and money. Nothing to do with me.
It's "mister", right? Good evening.
Huh? But wait, do you even work, mister?
Hey, mister. Doing all right?
Ugh... What a smell.
The smell is so foul, I forgot why I came.
I'll come back another time. Bye.
You again, mister?
You're a real odd one, mister.
Have you got a family, mister?
But I'm not jealous or anything.
'Cause having a family is way happier,
if you ask me.
Mister, are you a policeman or a detective?
Hello, mister. Come on in.
Even a child this small has to work...
Humans are admirable. They get by on
their own strength alone...
We can't exist without humans.
How ironic...
Give this servant any order you wish...
note: After '{NAME}, my master...' (M2#0); starts a new sentence.

en: I get the odd cut now and then,
but bruises are rare. Can't recall how.
Master, tell me what you require.
Somehow I just can't sleep well at night.
And my body's worn out, too. Strange, that.
Morning! You're an early riser, aren't you?
Ah, good morning.
You're not from around here.
Never seen your face before.
I'm Malcolm. I run the butcher's over there.
And you?
Pleased to meet you, Malcolm.
Sure thing, good to meet ya!
Right, time to put in another hard day's work.
You work hard at your job too, eh?
, it's you. Morning!
note: After the name: '{NAME}, it's you. Morning!' (as #101/#1784).

en: You're a steady one, always up early.
I'm off to buy in meat myself. See ya.
Morning! Lovely morning, eh?
Fine weather puts me in a good mood all day.
You're never too lively in the mornings, eh?
You're up early, but I reckon you're
really not a morning person. Well, chin up.
Oh, evening.
What's up, mate? Lost your way?
You don't look like you're from around here.
Yes. I have only just come to London.
But I am not lost.
Oh, I see, I see. Sorry, I jumped the gun.
note: Msg 202257 joins #4977 on the same line: variant with a trailing space.

variants.en: Oh, I see, I see. Sorry, I jumped the gun.

en: It's dark around here, so watch yourself.
Hey, hold on, at least tell me your name.
We're in the same city. We'll meet again.
I'm Malcolm, the butcher.
Well then...
Right, get home safe.
, it's you. Hey!
note: After the name: '{NAME}, it's you. Hey!' (as #1784).

en: Out here in those fancy clothes again?
note: Shared with msg 202350.

en: You must be real carefree or real gutsy.
Lots of workers round here. Some of 'em
note: Sentence runs over #4987/#4988 (shared with msg 202350, where #5059 replaces this row).

en: can't stand even seeing a man of good family
walk by. Don't come here much at night.
Hey, it's you. We meet again.
There's been some nasty business, so go easy
on the night walks.
Mind you, Jack the Ripper's
victims are all women, from what I hear.
If you get in trouble, shout for help.
Welcome, come on in!
What'll you have? Plenty of fresh meat here.
This is... a butcher's?
Well, well, what's this fella on about?
A tailor's with slabs of meat hanging up?
There's no such thing in this world!
I'm Malcolm, the owner. Order what you like.
I'll cut it to whatever size you want.
I see...
I smelled blood and couldn't help coming in.
(Oops, I let that slip.)
Ha ha, you've got quite a nose on you.
Well, no meat's cut without bleeding.
You'll have to put up with the smell.
Look, I went and cut my own hand just now.
Didn't get any on the goods, so don't worry.
Is that so...
Well, you should be careful.
Oh, it's you! I've been waiting for ya.
What'll it be? Got plenty of fresh meat.
I can't help noticing the smell of blood.
What, don't you want any meat?
Welcome!
note: Shared with Anita (msgs 406187/406449).

en: How about some meat for supper?
You've got a missus at least, right?
No, I'm afraid I live alone.
What? That's pitiful.
A ladies' man like you, still single?
You never buy meat, yet you come by a lot.
Got nobody who'll cook for you?
Poor fella. Why not come round my place?
My wife's a great cook.
Drop by sometime if you feel like it.
Oh, come on in.
I bet you're not buying anything, but fine.
Have a browse all the same.
Drop by my house too, I don't mind.
It's just round the corner from the shop.
Hey, what's up, mate?
Yeah, good to meet ya!
Oh, it's you.
Come by the shop and I'll give you a deal!
, it's you. What's up?
note: After the name (as #1843).

en: The butcher's isn't open right now.
As you can probably see.
You're looking into something, I hear, but I
can't do much to help you there.
Well, hang in there.
, it's you! Good of you to come.
How about it? Stay for a bite while you're here?
No, let's make it another time.
Aw, come on, don't be shy.
...Don't tell me you don't like meat?
Come on by whenever you're hungry.
Morning! Up early for a young fella. I'm impressed.
You're up very early yourself.
Oh, and polite to boot!
Pleased to meet you, Malcolm.
Yes, I'm still new to London.
But I'm not lost, I assure you.
Thank you. Until next time, then.
I hope we'll get along. Good night, then.
Hey,
You must be real carefree or real gutsy.
note: Same wording as #4985 (slice 062).

en: Lots of workers round here. Some of 'em
Good afternoon. Oh, so this is a butcher's?
I smelled blood and couldn't help coming in.
(Oh no! Will he suspect me?)
note: Thought after a pause; it continues on the same line as #5061 / #5067.

en: Some nose you've got there! I'm amazed.
I-is that so? Do take care of it...
I've just remembered an errand. Excuse me.
Good afternoon. I thought I'd drop by.
I notice the smell of blood more than meat.
Sadly, I'm still on my own.
A ladies' man like you!
Hurry up and find yourself a pretty wife!
Come by the shop and I'll give you a deal!
No, thank you kindly, but another time...
What's up? What brings you here this late?
Too late to browse the shop or grab a meal.
Malcolm, forgive me!
Wh-what's this, apologizing all of a sudden?
I have no time to spare.
Please, lend me your strength.
note: No used_in in the slice, but msg.py shows it after #5077 in msg 202890 (player, before biting Malcolm).

en: What the hell are you doing?! Aaagh!
What is your wish today...
note: Follows the #854 variant ', my master. ' on the same line: starts with a capital.

en: I feel so sluggish... and sleepy.
I'm all cut up, too... but oddly, it doesn't hurt.
It gives me the creeps.
I'll do as you wish...
note: Follows #0 ', my master...' on a new line.

en: I had a dream I was beating up women and kids.
That didn't really happen... did it?
Move aside, you. You're in the way.
I can't get by with you standing there.
I'm not used to these streets.
note: Stern player register (after 'Ah, forgive me.').

en: Huh, so you're a stranger here.
Just don't block the way.
Wander around too much and people'll get suspicious.
Fancy seeing you first thing in the morning.
Oh well. I'm off to work now.
Nothing's gone right lately, so honestly,
I'd been sulking.
But somehow I've got a feeling something good
is coming. I hope it really happens.
I would like to ask the way.
Sure, but I don't know the area that well.
I just go between the factory and home.
I don't go places I've no business in.
I see. So that's how it is.
And what sort of work do you do, may I ask?
What do you want to know that for?
You're a strange one.
I work at the factory. It's a lousy job.
What? You want something?
, it's you. Hi.
You seem livelier at night.
Me, I'm worn out after a day at the factory.
Even at home, all I do is eat and sleep.
Hey, how's it going? You well?
I'm not too tired today myself.
I wish it was always like this.
Work again tomorrow... Guess I'll keep at it.
You take care too. See you.
Hey, this is a factory. You can't come in here.
I didn't know I was not permitted to enter.
I don't care about apologies, just get
out of here. This is a match factory.
It's dangerous!
Sorry to have caused a commotion.
Oh, it's you. You can't be here, get out.
I keep telling you it's dangerous. You just don't get it, do you?
I keep telling you not to come in here.
The other workers were bothered too.
This is no place to wander into for fun.
...Look at my fingers.
They're half melted away, see?
The stuff we use for matches is poison.
Now that you know, clear off, will you?
Did someone say you could look around?
If you feel sick or anything happens, we
can't be held responsible, you know.
I bet you're rich.
Must be nice, living however you like.
I got myself a wife, sure, but life is
hard, and the work's rough... Haah.
Just here to gawk?
You must be idle. A rich man's pastime, is it?
Though there's a rumor you're a detective.
Who are you?
...Oh, from the mansion where Agnes works?
Huh, guess not.
You want something?
What's the reason you're
loitering around here?
I'd rather you didn't come to the factory,
but coming to my house is fine, I guess.
Fancy a rich man coming to a dump like this.
Well, have a look if it amuses you.
Try not to come by the factory too often.
Officially, it's off-limits to outsiders.
You're done with hard toil and poverty.
Live on as my servant...
Now, the battle begins. Watch and see...
Ah, I'm sorry.
I was getting my bearings as I walked.
Then do it at the side of the pavement.
I'd like to ask the way, if I may.
Sure, but I don't know the area that well.
I usually just go between factory and home.
Good afternoon. Is this place off-limits?
I'm terribly sorry.
...I see.
I understand. Sorry for the trouble.
So it was you. You can't be here, get out.

en: Yes, it is! I'm so glad I ran into you.
Thank you for the other day.
I know London's streets much better now.
I've walked all over the place.
Though I got lost plenty of times.
We meet again. How have you been?
I've fallen in love with the museum.
I'm there all day long.
Oh, good evening. Excuse me a moment.
Is there a museum near here?
Or is that biggest one the only one?
Hmm, I believe that may be the only one.
To be honest, I'm no expert myself.
Oh, I thought so. What a shame.
Then maybe next week I'll tour the galleries.
There are lots of painters sketching in town.
You're fond of the museum, then?
Yes, I am. I go almost every day.
I never get tired of looking.
I came to London to see the sights.
I see. May your trip be a pleasant one.
Thank you for earlier.
It's almost a bit cold tonight.
The days are quite mild, but the nights
get cold, don't they? Please take care
of yourself.
Strange,
note: Before the name + #7896 ", you're" + #10008: "Strange, {NAME}, you're / easy to spot even at night."

en: easy to spot even at night.
You draw the eye, or... no, it's that the
night suits you. Yes, I'm sure of it.
Hello? Is something the matter?
Huh? ...Oh, it's nothing.
Everything here is so new to me, I was
just lost in it, that's all.
I see. My apologies.
It seems I disturbed you by calling out.
Not at all.
My name is Anna. I'm visiting London
as a tourist.
This museum is really amazing.
I think I'll keep coming for a while.
Indeed, one day is not enough to see it all.
I hope you enjoy your trip.
Thank you. See you again.
We have in fact met before. Do you
recall, I wonder?
Disturb me? Not at all... Oh?
That's right, we met in town.
Meeting again... what a lovely twist of fate.
Anyway...
note: Standalone, because the next row #10020 also starts a sentence in msg 386006.

en: Take your time and enjoy it.
I never tire of it, no matter how often I look!
Oh, we meet again.
, so you like
museums too.
Yes, of course.
I am drawn to old and time-honored things.
So am I.
It's like touching history, and sometimes
it moves me deeply.
Oh, I'm so glad I came...
I wish I could stay here forever.
Ahaha, we meet again.
You'd think I'm here all day, wouldn't you?
Well, maybe that's not far from the truth.
I've really fallen in love with this place.
Though I'd like to see other places too.
When I graduate, I want to live in London.
Being a curator here would be wonderful.
I should have made my stay longer.
There are still places I haven't seen.
Oh, I wish I had more time.
Oh, what can I do for you?
You look much too grand for a cheap inn.
I'm just a tourist, you know.
I can't think what you'd want with me...
This place is pretty cheap. A real bargain.
Are you staying here too, by any chance?
Then they must have posher rooms too...
note: If he is a guest here too, the inn must have better rooms than hers.

en: , what's the matter?
note: After the name: "{NAME}, what's the matter?"

en: Ahaha, did you think you wouldn't find
me at the museum?
Don't worry, I'm there every day.
I hope we meet again at the museum.
Still, you and this inn are such an odd
match. It's funny.
I mean,
note: Before the name + #7896 ", you're" + #10068 (or #10095, slice 126, same text).

en: as refined as a nobleman, yet you think
nothing of coming to odd places. Ahaha.
I don't mind, so come by anytime.
Perhaps humans are drawn to history and
tradition because their lives are too short.
Then, as my servant,
I shall prolong that life of yours.
Now work for me to your heart's content.
I just wanted to take a different road.
I see. I hope you have a good trip.
I'm glad I could help. Well, goodbye.
Well, I think that's the only one.
To be honest, I don't know much about it either.
Are you fond of museums?
I see. I hope you have a good trip.
It'll be night soon, so do take care.
Thank you for the other day.
Excuse me? Is something the matter?
I see. I'm sorry.
It seems I disturbed you by calling out.
True, you can't see it all in one day.
I hope you enjoy your trip, Anna.
Excuse me? Is something wrong?
By the way, we've met before, haven't we?
Do you remember?
Take your time and enjoy it.
I'm drawn to old and time-honored things.
as refined as a nobleman, yet you think
note: Same as #10068 (slice 125): "I mean, {NAME}, you're / as refined as a nobleman, yet you think / nothing of coming to odd places. Ahaha."

en: I am Vanessa.
My husband and I run an inn
together.
My husband minds the place by day,
and that is why I sit here having tea,
you see. Ho ho...
Say, if you like, why not come and stay
at our inn?
For a gentleman as charming as you, I'd
offer all sorts of special services.
Ah, perhaps I shall call on it one day.
Where is this inn?
Just north of this café.
Our inn does rather good business.
I'm sure you would be satisfied.
I'm Vanessa, the owner of the inn.
Seeing me drink tea here every day, you
might think I'm neglecting my business,
but that isn't so at all.
Sitting here like this is part of
my work too... Heh heh heh...
Hello. I'm Vanessa, from the inn.
Here in London, there are so many
poor girls looking for work, aren't there?
I help girls like that find
a line of work.
Surviving alone in this city is hard
for a woman, after all...
Ho ho ho... Good day to you,
note: Name follows on the next line with #98 ".".

en: The world is full of people with no food
and nowhere to sleep, poor things.
To poor girls like that, I
offer a way to earn a living.
It's simple.
All they have to do is take a customer.
Then they get a meal and a bed for the night
at my inn. That's how it works.
Of course, the room and my finder's fee
I take as my share, mind you.
People, too, live by preying
on one another...
Don't you think so, too?
Welcome to the inn...
Please, make yourself at home.
How was it?
Do come again, won't you?
I'll be waiting for you again.
Do stay and relax a while.
We look forward to your next visit.
Who is it?
Haven't you got the wrong room?
Have you come to see me, perhaps?
You told me something once.
People, too, prey on each other to live,
you said...
Y-yes. I did say that, it's true.
Then, if people prey on one another,
for those people to become a vampire's prey
is only natural. Isn't that so?
Wh-what on earth are you saying?
I have no idea what you mean...
Ah! What are you doing?!
note: No used_in; Vanessa's cry when attacked (between msgs 390257 and 390293).

en: Aaaaagh!
note: No used_in; Vanessa's scream.

en: I seem to have made quite a capable
note: Continues in #10160 (slice 127): "human into my servant."

en: human into my servant.
note: Continues #10159 (slice 126) "I seem to have made quite a capable", as that report asks.

en: Hahahaha...
I'm Vanessa.
I run an inn.
I do hope we meet again.
Would you care to join me for tea?
How about tonight, perhaps?
At my inn, I'd offer you special services.
note: Innuendo kept (she runs the inn as a brothel).

en: I run the inn here,
and my name is Vanessa.
I'm off to mind the front desk at the inn.
Say, do come by my inn tonight,
won't you? Hm?
For a charming young man like you, I'd
offer all sorts of special services.
Hmm, maybe I'll stop by one of these days.
Just head north from this café
and you'll find it.
It's simple.
They stay the night with a gentleman, and
get a meal and a bed at my inn. That's all.
Welcome to the inn...
Please, tell me whatever you wish.
Am I working too hard? I feel dizzy.
But I'm hurt, and yet it doesn't hurt at all.
I'll do just as you command.
The woman next door and I both had bruises
on our faces. As if we'd been in a fistfight.
Um, excuse me...
Good morning, young lady.
Is there something you want of me?
Oh, um, you look like a fine gentleman, so
there's something I really must ask you.
...Would you have any work that I
could do?
Childcare, cleaning, laundry: I'll do anything.
Well, well, looking for work? How awkward.
I manage perfectly well on my own.
Why not try elsewhere?
I-I see...
Sorry for the bother. Please excuse me.
Um, my name is Beth.
If there's anything I can do, please tell
me... I'm begging you!
...I still haven't found any work...
At this rate, I can't make a decent living.
Good morning. Lovely morning, isn't it?
I've found a job!
Mind you, it's only for a month.
I'll do my best to make a life in London.
Good evening, um...
Good evening, young lady. What's the matter?
I'm sorry, um...
Would you have need of a maid or a nanny?
My name is Beth.
Could you take me on in your household?
Well, well, this is rather sudden.
I live alone, so I've no need of a nanny.
I can manage most things myself. Sorry.
I-I see...
I'm sorry for stopping you like that.
Excuse me...
I'm sorry about earlier...
Are you on your way home from work?
This may sound
rude of me, but
men are lucky to have so many kinds of work.
Even in London, the jobs a woman can earn
money at are few and far between. It's hard.
Oh, did I tell you that already?
It's cleaning a diner, but I'll do my best.
Sorry for all the trouble I caused you.
Good day, young lady. Pardon me.
I'll just take a book from the top shelf.
Oh! Ah, um, go right ahead.
What is the matter? You look downcast.
Though perhaps it's none of my business.
Not at all...
note: Answers "none of my business" (#10236).

en: I came to London to find work, and this
bookshop kindly took me on, but...
I'm being let go at the end of this week.
Times are hard, after all.
Oh my, that is unfortunate.
But I know of no work I could find you.
No, of course not...
Starting tomorrow, I'll look for a new job.
Please put the book back when you're done.
...Sigh...
You said you were looking for work,
but it seems you work here.
Well, about that...
I'll keep on looking for work.
If you know of a good job, please tell me.
I've only got three days left to live.
note: Hyperbole: her job ends in 3 days (fired at the end of the week).

en: You mustn't say such things.
Surely there is plenty of work as a maid or nanny.
Without experience, nobody will hire me.
Before London, I helped out on a farm,
but that's no use here.
I tried the employment agency too, but
I just can't find a good job.
...What am I to do...
There were a few men at the agency, too.
I was surprised. It's hard for everyone.
I came to London without thinking...
But I'll keep looking a little longer.
At the agency I saw people who lean on
others and do nothing for themselves,
and I thought, I mustn't be like that.
I did think of going home
to work on the farm, but...
But, but,
I've found a new job now,
so I'll try a little longer.
Oh, is it about a job, by any chance?
Whatever do you mean?
I only came to pay my respects.
Oh... Ah, I'm sorry!
P-pardon me, I'm sorry. Goodbye.
I'm sorry about earlier.
I'm looking for work, you see...
After work I walked about job-hunting,
so I'm worn out today...
Sorry, please let me rest...
I'm doing well, thanks to you.
I've found a new job at last. I'm happy.
Cleaning, washing, I'll do anything!
Please come again!
Is there something I can do for you?
Oh dear... You're looking for work?
I can manage most things on my own.
Why not try somewhere else?
Oh, that's rather sudden.
I live alone, so I've no need of a nanny,
and I can do most things myself. Sorry.
May I take a book from the top shelf?
What's wrong? You look downcast.
I see... That's a shame.
I can't think of any job to offer you.
Starting tomorrow, I'll look for a new job.
Oh, it's you, Beth.
You said you were looking for work,
but you're working here, aren't you?
Even a not-so-good one would do...
note: Follows #10252 (msg 395141): 'If you know of a good job...' / 'Even a not-so-good one would do...'.

en: Don't lose heart. Keep at it.
Isn't there plenty of work as a maid or nanny?
What do you mean?
I'm sorry, just when you'd found a job.
But I, too,
had a job for you to do.
Not that it's a job only you
could do.
But you must do it for me, too.
Help me... won't you.
note: Player (gentle register), bite scene; no speaker tag in the message.

en: How long must I keep doing this?!
note: Player's lament after the bite (msg 395458).

en: I'm the master's slave now,
so go on, give me any order you like.
Getting up of a morning's oddly hard.
...Too much drink, eh? Hah.
Give this old woman any order you please.
What's all this? My whole body hurts!
Has some fool been beating this old woman?
Hm? Who are you?
Aha, an errand boy from the liquor shop?
I paid off my tab the other day, didn't I?
I am not from the liquor shop.
Hah! So you're saying you greeted me
for no reason at all? You're an odd one.
Oh, never mind. Too much bother to ask.
I'm a busy woman, so I'll be off now.
What? You want something with me?
Well, I wondered what dimwit it was. It's you.
Don't go strutting about like that.
Some of us struggle just to get by each day.
This world sure is unfair.
, hold on a minute.
note: After the name at line start: 'Chris, hold on a minute.'

en: Good timing. Morning to you.
If only a fellow with deep pockets like you
would move into my lodging house.
No meals, mind, but I'd spare you a drink.
Pardon the intrusion.
What do you want? ...Hic.
If you know it's rude, don't ask. Hic.
Have you seen anyone suspicious around here?
...Not that you'd know, I suppose.
Hmph! Stop me, then insult me? How rude!
Be kinder to your elders. Hic.
Don't you make a fool of me... Hic.
...Pardon me.
Well! What an attitude! Hic.
Ask me whatever you like, I won't answer.
Hic... Urp.
You've got time to kill, roaming all over town.
Dunno what you do for a living, mind.
Well, good luck to you.
Oh, it's you. You keeping well?
Even I give a decent greeting
now and then, you know.
I'm glad to see you in good health.
You're an odd man, you are.
Nothing I say ever gets you down.
You must be somebody important, eh?
Ow! Watch where you're going!
Bumping into an old woman. Apologize!
Ah, my apologies.
Are you hurt, old woman?
Who're you calling old? Call me Madeline.
Honestly, I nearly dropped the liquor
I just bought!
Pardon me, then.
Though you seem to be drunk already...
note: No speaker tag; the player's (stern) line, parallel to gentle #10421.

en: What? What's wrong with drinking what I earn?
Quit your nagging.
...Oh, it's you.
What's wrong with drinking in the daytime?
Is there a law says "No drinking by day"?
Oh my. You're fond of a drink too, I see.
I'm much the same.
Old as I am, I drink every day.
Some fools preach, "It's poison for you,"
but at my age, what good is saving
money? I'll drink and enjoy myself.
That work of yours sounds hard.
I hear you've been asking around.
Now, wringing rent out of lodgers like I do,
that's a good job. Easy work.
Oh, we meet again.
Seems you only drink wine,
note: Wine: the vampire's usual cover drink.

en: but I know some fine liquor. Shall I tell you?
Ahh, I'm worn out.
At times like this, a drink's the thing.
Who are you? Looking for lodgings?
No rooms free right now.
What?
Don't tell me you're from the liquor shop?
I paid my tab already. Off with you.
You just don't get it, do you.
I've got no business with you.
You look like you've got money.
How nice it'd be if you were my lodger.
You'd pay your rent on time, I bet.
Come chat with this old girl now and then,
why don't you? I'll stand you a drink or so.
To be forced to wither into decrepitude...
note: Player, stern register (bite scene, msg 398635).

en: How pitiful humans are...
But if, even so, you still wish to cling
to life, then very well.
I shall grant you that wish.
and live on a while longer.
note: After #2010 'Become my servant,'; a pause follows, then #10409.

en: In that aged body of yours.
I'm not from the liquor shop.
note: Gentle parallel of #10325.

en: I only wanted to say hello.
Good evening. Pardon me a moment.
note: Madeline answers 'If you know it's rude, don't ask.' (#10342).

en: Have you seen anyone suspicious around here?
note: Same wording as stern #10343.

en: ...I don't suppose you'd know.
note: The slight that #10345 'Stop me, then insult me?' reacts to.

en: ...Pardon me. Until next time.
Good evening, Madeline.
I'm glad to see you looking so well.
Oh, I'm so sorry.
Are you hurt, granny?
note: 'granny' so #10366 'Who're you calling old? Call me Madeline.' answers it (slice 129 request).

en: I'm truly sorry.
Though you seem to be drunk already...
note: Same as stern #10370.

en: Good afternoon. Excuse me, is anyone in?
For your sake, I would
do anything at all...
This is a hat shop for fine ladies.
Are you after a gift for your sweetheart?
What sort of hats are in fashion now?
Let me see. Lace-trimmed hats
with wide brims are popular.
You're looking for a gift for a lady,
aren't you...
Do take your time and look around.
Ah, any lady who's given a hat by
a handsome gentleman like you...
how happy she must be!
What sort of beautiful lady could she be,
note: #9827 'I wonder...' follows.

en: Have you decided on a present yet?
No...
I don't have anyone in particular in mind,
so I'm in no hurry.
Oh my. And yet you've been coming here
almost every day...
Could it be... you've taken a fancy to me?
I can no longer hold back
these feelings of mine...
I do believe I've fallen
in love with you...
Since I fell for you, even the wind
and the rain all sound like lovely music
to my ears...
Had I been born a dog,
I could love you more honestly than now.
I have a feeling...
and I
note: After the name at line start: '{NAME} and I'.

en: are bound by the red thread of fate...
Relax. I'm sure the knot is a loose one.
The shop is about to close...
...Oh, I understand.
You've gone out of your way
to come and see me!
I'm so glad you came to see me.
Hee hee.
Coming here at such an hour...
Is it to ask me out on a date?
I see.
Despite your looks, you're quite the shy
type, aren't you.
Any time you'd like to make a date,
note: #7075 'I'll be waiting for you.' follows.

en: ...Yes, that's right.
Would you care for this lace-trimmed hat,
note: #3891 'perhaps?' follows on the next line.

en: Or this one, trimmed with ribbons.
...Oh, sir! It suits you wonderfully.
I'm not the one who'll be wearing it...
Speaking of beauty, Lady Rose of the
Epstein family also honors this shop
with her patronage.
She's a truly lovely lady, you know.
Some new hats came in yesterday...
I'm sure they'd suit you perfectly...
...This is a ladies' hat shop, isn't it?
I may not look it, but I am a man.
But I truly think they would suit you
ever so well.
The pink lace is just adorable.
Among fine ladies and young noblewomen,
our hats are very popular, you know.
Why, the famed beauty... the Epstein family's
Miss Rose loves our hats too.
I simply must have you wear
a certain dress for me.
As I keep telling you, I'm a man!
When it comes to beauty, man or woman
makes no difference...
When it comes to wearing a dress, it does
make a difference, I'd think...
Please, I beg you.
Just once, won't you try on a dress
for me...?
No, I must politely decline.
Please come again tomorrow.
I'll be waiting for you tomorrow.
I've already closed the shop...
If there's a hat you like,
I'll gladly set it aside for you.
You're
, aren't you?
How did you know?
I know, you see.
Why you've come here
note: followed by three '.' pause rows (#265) and #863 variant '' -> 'Why you've come here...'

en: You wanted to wear a dress,
so you came here, didn't you?
No, that's not it.
note: night scene, stern player register (#10507-#10519 have no used_in; msg 402953)

en: There's no need to be shy.
Everyone longs for beautiful things.
It's only natural.
Very well.
I'll change into that dress, so
would you put out the light...
All right.
Now, let me help you change.
Ah, what...?
Eeeeek...!
Good grief, I was nearly put through
note: no speaker tag; read as the player after Clio's scream

en: a dreadful ordeal...
Ask whatever you will of me.
Give me any order you please.
My, my! What a handsome man you are!
Sir, yours isn't the sort of face one sees in a
back-street liquor shop like this.
Whatever whim brought you here,
do buy a bottle before you go.
Everyone needs a drink in this life, sir.
Say, sir, lately the whole town's whispering of
note: wording agreed with slice 132 (#10569 'Lately the whole town's been whispering of'); #10534 shared

en: a killer who slashes folk. Have you heard?
Seems the bodies get carved up with a knife,
and folk have given the killer a nickname:
"Jack the Ripper."
With a murderer like that on the prowl,
I'm too scared to set foot outside at night.
That knife murderer still hasn't been caught,
it seems.
What on earth are the police doing?
Hopeless, the lot of 'em!
Just how frightened us common folk are -
I bet they've no idea.
Oh my, I've gone and got carried away.
Do buy a drop of something before you go.
Say, sir, have you heard?
Lady Rose, Count Epstein's daughter.
She's ever so beautiful, she is.
What sort of man will end up marrying her,
I wonder.
Every notable in London wants to take her
as his bride, from what I hear...
Lady Rose of the Epstein family - a beauty
like her, I've never seen in all my days.
You often hear tales of folk made unhappy
by their good looks...
But folk made unhappy by being plain are far
more numerous, I'm sure.
My, my! What a handsome young man!
Sir, a man of your breeding doesn't come to a
back-street liquor shop like this, does he?
I don't know what whim brought you here,
but since you've come, do buy something
before you go, won't you?
Everyone needs a drink in this life, you know.
Especially poor folk like us.
Lately the whole town's been whispering of
note: #10534 (slice 131, shared with #10533) must continue: 'a killer who slashes folk. Have you heard?'

en: You're after her too, aren't you, sir?
Ah ha ha! No need to blush.
She seems to be fast asleep.
Now's my chance...
What d'you think you're doing!
note: Anita talking in her sleep

en: Mmm... Old man,
stop wriggling around so much.
I can't get to sleep...
It seems she hasn't actually woken up.
Well then...
note: no speaker tag; read as the player

en: At night, please lend me your help...
